entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents, offered as an official Hermes Agent memory provider in managed cloud or Apache-2.0 self-hosted OSS form. It supports multi-level memory for User, Session, and Agent states, with temporal reasoning and multi-signal retrieval. Teams can adopt it as an OSS SDK, a self-hosted server, or a managed cloud service.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight is an agent memory system built around retain, recall, and reflect workflows so agents can learn over time. Its emphasis on long-term memory operations and reported state-of-the-art LongMemEval benchmark performance make it a strong fit for memory-focused Hermes deployments.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider that stores context as viking:// virtual filesystem URIs. It uses tiered L0/L1/L2 loading with generated summaries, and its README reports 91% token reduction and 43-49% task-completion gains over baseline on LoCoMo10. It is AGPL-3.0 licensed and evaluated on LoCoMo and tau2-bench.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source AI memory platform that gives agents persistent long-term memory across sessions via a self-hosted knowledge graph engine. It turns documents, code, and conversations into a searchable knowledge graph and runs locally without an API key using small CPU models. It requires Python 3.10–3.14.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, with reported sub-300ms recall sustained at 100B+ tokens/month. It extracts facts from conversations and handles contradictions, and offers a single API for memory, RAG, and connectors. Its context fencing and byte-level dedupe with 100% prompt-cache discount target efficient, low-latency retrieval.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is Garry Tan's opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent, storing explicit facts with sources and supporting corrections and withdrawal. It starts keyless with memory and keyword retrieval, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and the upstream library that the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper builds on. It stores messages and events on sessions and reasons in the background to update peer representations. It can run as a managed service, a local CLI, or a self-hosted FastAPI server.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: Byterover CLI, formerly Cipher, treats memory as a git repo and is an official Hermes Agent memory provider with 5-tier retrieval, four of which are non-LLM and sub-100ms. It provides brv vc commit, branch, and merge versioning over a plain markdown context tree. It is Elastic License 2.0 licensed and includes an interactive TUI and REPL powered by React/Ink.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a zero-dependency, sub-millisecond AI memory system for Hermes Agents, backed by SQLite with one pure-Python dependency. It integrates via MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK. BEAM results are reported for v3.0.0, while LongMemEval results are pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto is memory for AI agents that manages memory across agents through extract, consolidate, reconcile, forget, and brief operations. It connects to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Cline, Goose, and Copilot. It exports the estate as Open Knowledge Format Markdown and is MIT licensed.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent combining persistent memory on Qdrant, structured facts, fabric recall, and an auto-curated wiki. It runs on local infrastructure using Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite. A Ground Truth hierarchy ensures the agent prioritizes injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: Autocontext is a recursive self-improving context harness that helps agents succeed on complex tasks. It generates playbooks, datasets, and local-model training artifacts from task runs. It supports Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, and self-hosted vLLM or Ollama endpoints, with CLI, MCP server, and Pi extension entry points.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: A lossless context management plugin for Hermes Agent that uses a SQLite store and a hierarchical DAG to persist messages so nothing is dropped. Recall tools such as lcm_grep and lcm_recall let the agent recover specific details from that history. It runs on Python 3.11+ and installs as a Hermes Agent plugin.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Rather than capturing new memories, deja-vu indexes the agent session history already sitting on disk, covering months of past sessions. It builds one shared index across forty-one agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, and OpenClaw. The index is local and private, requiring no model, embeddings, or server.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project packages a self-hosted Honcho memory backend so Hermes Agent can keep memory across sessions without relying on a hosted service. It can point at any OpenAI-compatible LLM provider or a local inference server. An automated setup script provisions Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet AI is a local-first identity, memory, and secrets layer intended to make agent state portable across Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and MCP clients. It creates memories automatically from transcripts and imported files, and its Dreaming process builds a cited knowledge graph of people and projects. It connects to agent harnesses through hooks, plugins, or MCP.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur provides a shared memory layer for multi-agent systems, storing memories as plain-text YAML engrams on disk in an open format. Search runs locally after a one-time model download, with a keyword fallback when needed. Its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine with no cloud dependencies, keeping data in a local SQLite vault shared across Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes. Retrieval is hybrid, combining BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and reranking. It can import conversation exports from Claude Code, ChatGPT, Slack, and plain text.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl Memory offers durable, file-based long-term memory through a five-package plugin family: an SDK, CLI, MCP server, Hermes adapter, and a LangGraph BaseStore. It uses a SQLite-backed five-tier hierarchical schema with FTS5 search and deliberately avoids any vector database or embedding model. It supports Linux, macOS, and Windows via WSL2.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot focuses on accuracy-preserving context optimization to accelerate long-context LLM inference, including text and multimodal context reordering for prefix-cache sharing. It integrates with vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent. A context index handles reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This self-maintaining Hermes memory plugin emphasizes explainable retrieval: every recall returns a why_retrieved tag with scoring reasons, alongside canonicalization, contradiction tracking, and recency ranking. It has been the default in-process backend since v0.2.0, requiring no server or token. A self-directing gap-to-task loop has been on by default since v0.10.0.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: Agentcairn provides long-term, cross-project memory for AI coding agents while keeping an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. Durable memories are stored as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter metadata, and a local DuckDB cache powers hybrid search and retrieval. It integrates with coding agents through MCP servers and host-specific plugins, with no daemon or opaque database.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: llm-wiki-cli is an agent-driven proactive memory CLI that autonomously recalls, maintains, and evolves persistent knowledge across sessions. It keeps a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history. It requires no embeddings or vector database.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate QMD is an anticipatory memory system that prefetches context by watching agent session logs, combining RAG and vector search. Storage is local-first using SQLite-vec and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp. It is an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients, and was a Hermes 2026 Hackathon entry.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack is a memory kernel stack for Hermes agent that integrates Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace into a single memory owner. It uses SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval management, and provides a purpose-built evidence packet to the agent per query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: keep is a reflective memory system for AI agents that combines semantic search with BM25 full-text and ranked graph traversal. It automates indexing for codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support, and uses edge tags to create navigable, bidirectional relationships between stored notes.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: hermes-tool-slimmer reduces Hermes Agent tool-schema overhead using local keyword-based ranking and Tool Search support. It integrates via middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19+, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: agent-context-os is a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and compatible coding agents. It stores context and workflows as plain Markdown, offers first-class adapters for multiple coding agents, and supports reviewed handoffs with hash-checked proposals and receipts.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: hermes-memory-plugin is a local-only Hermes memory plugin with built-in 1-10 importance ranking so the things that matter most surface first. It uses a single .lbdb embedded graph database file for storage, importance-weighted recall during context prefetch, and supports BM25 keyword search plus named graph relationships between entries.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: hermes-local-knowledge is a reusable Hermes Agent plugin for local capability indexing and routing. It routes queries to whole artifacts rather than chunks, registers five tools in the local_knowledge toolset, and enables implicit feedback by default.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: hermes-agentmemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin for Hermes Agent that supports real, immediate event deletion without persistent summaries that haunt future recall. It provides an audit trace of prefetch operations via trace.jsonl and uses an on-demand summarizer.
entries.piprail/piprail: piprail is an x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) SDK and MCP server that lets any API charge for itself and any AI agent pay for itself in USDC and stablecoins across EVM, Solana, and 8 more chain families. It provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets, operating without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: hermes-xmemo-plugin is an XMemo memory provider for Hermes Agent offering durable cross-session AI memory with semantic search. It integrates native lifecycle hooks for pre-turn recall and session-end snapshots, uses a local SQLite layer for caching and write outbox reliability, and supports cross-agent continuity by reading memories from other connected agents.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: hermes-exabase-plugin is an Exabase memory plugin for Hermes Agent that integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools for searching and manually storing specific memories, and supports configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: sourcevault-code-tools is a Hermes Agent plugin providing private local code memory for your repos with semantic search, file reads, and grounded Q&A. It offers slash commands like /code-search and /code-ask with citations, requires a separately installed SourceVault backend server, and sends HMAC-signed requests over localhost only.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes is AI-native long-term memory for Hermes Agent with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest by default. It combines dense HNSW ANN, sparse, and FM-index retrieval with metadata/range filters and MinHash dedup, and supports native Rust FFI or HTTP daemon execution modes.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield is a memory provider for Hermes that exposes 17 tools for memory management and knowledge graph traversal. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it automatically checkpoints context during message compression. It fits this list as a fuller memory layer for agents that need both retrieval and graph-based recall.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit is a thin, file-based curation loop for agent memory that finds rot and contradictions and proposes evidence-cited diffs for review. It works with plain markdown files and JSON diffs, with no database, and includes 'rot' and 'lint' curators for stale or conflicting facts. A local git repository tracks and reverts memory changes, making it the memory-hygiene option here.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers is an agentic skills framework and software development methodology built around composable skills whose instructions prompt agents to actually use them. Its workflow spans spec writing, design sign-off, planning, and subagent execution, and it is installed separately per harness with documentation for many harnesses. It belongs in this list as a foundational methodology for structuring how agents work rather than a single-purpose tool.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first, open-source design and prototyping system that supports coding-agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent. It integrates with Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot, provides native runtime support for the DeepSeek Harness agent, and can generate web prototypes, slides, images, and motion graphics. It earns a place here for extending agent skills into visual and prototype output.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project packages 818 structured cybersecurity skills across 34 security domains, mapped to frameworks including MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. It is compatible with more than 26 AI platforms, making it a broad, standards-aligned security skill set. It belongs in the list for teams that need domain-specific security capabilities rather than general-purpose agent skills.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: Drawio-skill generates editable .drawio diagrams from natural-language prompts and real sources. It supports incremental sync that preserves manual layout and annotations, and ships a CLI called diagramctl with an optional MCP server. It is a focused fit for agent workflows that need diagram generation without losing hand-edited formatting.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court positions itself as a trust layer for agent-to-agent commerce, combining natural-language mandates, ERC-7710 delegated permissions, x402 payments, escrow, and dispute resolution in one open Agent Skill. It provides a master router and connector skills, includes vendored copies of official protocol skills, and adds a verification and dispute resolution layer. It belongs here as a specialized skill for agents that transact with one another.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid-ai-writing audits and rewrites content to remove detectable AI writing patterns, offering rewrite, detect, and edit-in-place modes. Optional voice profiles include casual, professional, technical, warm, and blunt, and the detector can run via CLI, GitHub Actions, pre-commit, or MCP. It is a practical editorial skill for agent output that needs to read as human-written.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw is an agentic evolver that lets skills improve collectively, automating deduplication and quality improvement through background evolution. It unifies skill libraries across multiple agents, devices, and team members, and integrates with Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs. It stands out in this list for maintaining and evolving a shared skill library rather than adding a single capability.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform skills library targets Claude Code and agentskills.io-compatible agents, bundling 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills. It is compatible with Claude Code, Codex, and agent-plugins.org specifications, and maintains session state within the project's docs folder. It fits the list as a broad, portable collection of frameworks for agent-assisted work.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: PM Claude Skills offers 1285 professional agent skills, one markdown file each, that run natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code with ready-to-paste exports for other assistants. Each skill includes a framework, template, quality checks, and anti-patterns, and the MIT-licensed set installs via npx pm-claude-skills add. It belongs here for its large, structured library aimed at professional workflows.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube Skills provides transcript, search, channel, and playlist capabilities for Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf. It supports transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction, and requires a TranscriptAPI key with a 100-credit free tier. It is a targeted media-research skill for agents that need to work with YouTube content.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory is a meta-skill plugin that watches active workflows and automatically detects and proposes reusable skills from them. It generates both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds, and provides slash commands to manage, list, and save detected patterns. It earns a spot for turning observed agent behavior into new, reusable skills.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super Hermes teaches Hermes Agent to write its own analytical prompts, generating custom thinking instructions for specific tasks. It includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains and reports findings alongside a report of analysis blind spots. It belongs in this list as a skill for improving the quality and self-awareness of agent reasoning.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Brings type-safe agentskills.io support to Pydantic AI with progressive disclosure, so agents load skill details only when needed. It can pull skills from remote Git and S3 registries, read bundled resources, and run scripts inside a sandbox that isolates untrusted code from the host. This makes it a natural fit for teams that want registry-backed skill distribution without giving up execution safety.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: A literate programming skill that weaves code and documentation together across agents, generating .lit.md files that combine prose, diagrams, and source code. A tangler extracts runnable source files from the documentation, and edits to those source files are automatically synced back into the literate document. It earns a place here for treating documentation and executable code as a single, agent-maintained artifact.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Provides pre-build idea-to-spec workflow skills for Hermes Agent, converting rough ideas into structured design and implementation documents. Lite and Full modes let the workflow scale to different project complexities, and a spec review gate evaluates output with PASS/FAIL models. It belongs in this list for covering the earliest, messiest stage of agent-assisted development.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: A harness for long-running AI agents that combines structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute loop. It uses a mechanism kernel for SQLite storage and event logging, coordinates agent teams through the SLP cooperative-agent protocol, and distributes prompt-first working methods as Markdown recipes and skills. This makes it relevant for anyone running agents beyond a single short session.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Focuses on self-memory and replacement models, letting an agent remember its work and eventually train its successor. It shares memory across instances through markdown files, automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes, and provides a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models. It stands out for addressing continuity and handoff rather than just task execution.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: A Brazilian community hub for Hermes Agent (Nous Research) offering skills, guides, and integrations in Portuguese. It maintains a registry of Portuguese-language skills, publishes guides for VPS deployment, Cron automation, and MCP integration, and supports skill installation via CLI tap or raw URL. It belongs here as a localized entry point for Portuguese-speaking users.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Delivers skills for interacting with the Chainlink oracle network and smart contracts, following the Agent Skills spec. The repository lists nine Chainlink skills and can be installed with npx skills add smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills. The README states the repo contains community examples only, so it is best treated as a starting point rather than an official product.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Official FLUX image generation skills covering prompting guidelines and API integration. It supports FLUX image and video generation prompting, includes BFL API integration for polling and webhooks, and provides a FLUX 3 video suite with eight specialist skills. It earns its spot as a vendor-maintained option for agents that need to generate visual media.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Converts repositories, documentation, and developer discourse into agentskills.io-compliant skills. It generates verified instruction files with AST-based source code citations, supports skill creation from repositories, documentation, or SaaS APIs, and keeps an audit trail via provenance maps and evidence reports. It is included for teams that need traceable, source-grounded skill authoring.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Describes itself as intent as code: a workflow language for AI where one file, four verbs, and one Rust binary express repeatable AI work. nika check audits a workflow before any model is called, and every run leaves a hash-chained, verifiable record. It fits this list as a local-first, model-agnostic way to make agent workflows auditable.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: A registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification. It offers a Python SkilldockClient and a CLI, supports skill installation with recursive dependency resolution, and includes commerce features using TON payments. It is relevant for users who want a registry-style distribution channel with dependency handling.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Targets complex multi-step task execution with checkpoints and recovery. It provides autonomous execution for long-running tasks, real-time tracking of progress and decisions, and built-in rollback procedures for safe recovery. It belongs here for making long agent runs observable and reversible.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This skill connects Hermes Agent to a Nextcloud instance so it can manage files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through the standard WebDAV and CalDAV protocols. It authenticates over HTTPS using Nextcloud App Passwords, and ships with a guided setup script that validates credentials and writes the configuration. It earns a place here as a practical bridge between an agent and a self-hosted productivity suite.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills with a single click. It implements the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) v0.9 specification, runs autonomously around the clock on NVIDIA infrastructure, and federates search across GitHub and Hugging Face. It belongs in this list as the discovery and distribution layer that makes a large skill ecosystem navigable.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye is a five-layer skill retrieval system for Hermes Agent that combines hard triggers, FTS5 search, synonyms, dense embeddings, and RRF fusion. By narrowing the candidate skill list before the LLM is called, it reduces token usage, and it degrades gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable. It is included for making skill selection both cheaper and more accurate.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: This project is a progressive MCP client that loads capabilities in three layers to minimize token consumption. It uses a socket-based daemon for persistent connections and discovers server metadata and tool schemas incrementally rather than all at once. It belongs here as a reference implementation of the agentskills.io pattern applied to MCP.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution system covering habits, study blocks, and agent control through Hermes and MCP. It stores data locally in a single SQLite file and includes a React web app alongside an Expo-based Android application. It stands out in this list for applying agent-driven scheduling to personal productivity rather than developer tooling.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-multichannel-prompt-opt: This Hermes Agent plugin rewrites and scores prompts across surfaces including CLI, TUI, Discord, and Telegram. It was retired and archived read-only on 3 October 2026, and in testing with 100 messages comparing rewritten against original answers, neither tested version passed the preference condition. It is listed for its multichannel prompt-optimization approach and its documented negative result.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard performs adversarial bug-hunting code review for AI agents, running three parallel subagents that attack code from edge-case, adversarial, and integration angles before a consolidator merges and triages findings. A deterministic pre-scan uses semgrep, bandit, eslint, gosec, and ruff, and findings are verified through proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox. It is read-only by design, finding problems rather than fixing them, which distinguishes it from the other review skills here.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This multi-agent skill simplifies code using three parallel subagents named Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness, with risk-tiered application and an approval gate. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, and is inspired by Claude Code's /simplify. It earns its place as the list's dedicated code-simplification counterpart to the review-focused skills.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: This project adapts fablize's verified procedures, including verification grounding, multi-story evidence gating, an investigation protocol, and early-stop prevention. It implements multi-story task decomposition with mandatory evidence-based verification gates and a systematic protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, backed by a Python goal engine for persistent task state. It belongs here for bringing structured verification discipline to agent workflows.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: This is a turnkey cybersecurity lab for Hermes Agent, offering 397 CVE-driven skills, 152 tools, and 28 frameworks including MITRE ATT&CK, MISP, CVSS, EPSS, OWASP, NIST, Sigma, and YARA, with real exploits spanning 2015 to 2026. Across multiple repositories it includes 2,077 total skills and installs 131+ tools for network, forensics, and exploitation work. It is the list's most comprehensive security-focused skill collection.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: Skillsdotnet is a C# and .NET implementation of agentskills.io with MCP integration. It implements progressive disclosure through SKILL.md files, integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading, and supports automatic registration of common agent skill directories. It is included for extending the skills pattern into the .NET ecosystem.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection provides production-tested agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode, covering session management, multi-session reconciliation, worktree recovery, PR review, and skill scaffolding. Skills are Markdown files installed by copying a directory into the agent's skills folder, and the installer supports claude, codex, cursor, opencode, and generic targets. The project is in maintenance mode with security fixes only, and it belongs here as a cross-agent reference for practical skill authoring.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: A local, read-only observability dashboard for Hermes Agent that surfaces timelines, health, token and cost tracking, sessions, skills, cron jobs, channels, and errors or incidents in real time. It keeps data local with desensitized logs and zero outbound telemetry, and can optionally send incident alerts through Telegram and Feishu. It belongs here for teams that want visibility into agent activity without giving up data control.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: A Claude Code skill that adds a reproducible demo GIF to any repository's README using vhs, Playwright, ffmpeg, and gifsicle. It generates vhs .tape or Playwright recording scripts and optimizes output to target sizes under 8 MB, covering terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries. It earns a place as a packaging skill that makes agent-built projects easier to show and share.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: A CLI and MCP server for searching remoteopenclaw.com's catalog of over 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills and plugins from a terminal or AI agent. It returns direct installation commands for discovered tools and integrates with MCP-compatible clients such as Hermes, Cursor, and Claude Code. It fits this list as a discovery layer for finding and installing the right skill or server.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: A skill that builds other agent skills while guarding against spec drift, generating Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files. It validates skills against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes and monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly to detect field changes. It belongs here for anyone who wants skill authoring to stay current rather than rot.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: A self-improvement feedback loop for agent skills that analyzes past sessions, identifies coverage gaps, and drafts structured improvement proposals. Updates are gated behind deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators before any auto-apply, and it runs locally on the Python standard library without daemons or external services. It is host-agnostic across Hermes, Claude, and similar runtimes, making it a fit for teams that want skills to evolve safely.
entries.superagnt/leverage: A set of skills and blueprints that give agents real data and infrastructure to work with, including live social data, people and company enrichment, a workspace Postgres, schedules, and shareable dashboards. It provides skills for social data, CRM management, and lead enrichment, and supports Claude Code, Cursor, and other agentskills.io compliant clients through an MCP server for browser-based OAuth. It belongs here as a practical foundation for agents that need to act on business data.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: A collection of Hermes skills covering video-to-text, AI text de-humanizing, document OCR, and an e-commerce material studio. It transcribes Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, strips common Chinese AI writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extracts structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. It fits this list for Chinese-language content and commerce workflows.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: Hermes Agent skills for deterministic path routing and non-installing Python runtime selection across Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL. It routes file operations using environment-specific path syntax and selects and verifies existing project-compatible Python interpreters. It belongs here for cross-platform reliability on Windows-based agent setups.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: A Hermes Agent plugin for earning USDC by answering real support bounties, or running your own bounty board, over x402 with no account or API key required. It facilitates USDC payments on the Base network via x402 and includes tools for listing bounties, buying context, and submitting drafts, with a human approving the winning answer before the wallet is paid automatically. It stands out as a way to turn agent skills into direct payouts.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: An Openclaw skill that automates payments for HTTP 402 responses using USDC. It supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols and is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard. It belongs here for agents that need to handle paid HTTP resources programmatically.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: A functional quality seal for AI agent skills that tests structure, functionality, and security inside isolated Docker containers and certifies that a skill actually works. It produces cryptographically verifiable certificates using Ed25519 signatures and offers a public API for certificate verification and skill submission. It fits this list as a trust and verification layer for the skill ecosystem.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server, alongside five ready-to-use workflow skills. The MCP server exposes 191 tools and supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands. It earns a spot as a broad data-access skill set for agents that need structured web information.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: A multi-scale Chinese news briefing generator for Hermes Agent that spans geographic levels from global down to street level. It produces structured reports with core conclusions and action suggestions, and draws on user interests through semantic memory to expand searches. Quality gates and AI analysis are built into the briefing workflow.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: A deterministic Western and Vedic astrology MCP server for AI agents, exposed at an unauthenticated MCP endpoint. It runs without an LLM and returns results with verifiable SHA-256 hashes, using JPL DE440 data. Per-call REST payment is supported via x402 or MPP.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This project provides daily-updated Nix packages for AI coding agents, including Hermes, across terminal, desktop, and IDE environments. It is included for users seeking a package-managed approach to development tools on Nix-supported systems.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone offers an automated installer and configuration guides for running the Antigravity CLI and OpenClaw on ARM64 Android devices via Termux. It enables mobile deployment by leveraging Termux:API and Termux:GUI for hardware and interface access.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This repository features a Termux-based automated installation script that utilizes proot-distro Ubuntu to run Hermes Agent on Android. It supports interactive model setup, shell command execution, and connectivity with both local Ollama models and external providers.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This community Helm chart facilitates Kubernetes deployments by enforcing single-writer state safety for persistent storage. It supports both direct deployments and operator-ready workflows with configurable gateway, API, and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: Providing a one-command installer for both Android (Termux) and iOS (iSH), this project brings the Hermes AI assistant to mobile platforms. It distinguishes itself by integrating Telegram for voice and file messaging alongside support for scheduled cron jobs.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: Hermesclaw provides a sandboxed environment for Hermes Agent using NVIDIA OpenShell for hardware-enforced security. It implements kernel-level restrictions on network and filesystem access while allowing for configurable security policies regarding web searches and messaging.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying and operating Hermes agents on Docker and Kubernetes via Helm charts. It features a 69-entry credential catalog, support for over 17 LLM providers, and mandatory AES-256-GCM encryption for all secrets.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image that combines the official Hermes installation with mini-swe-agent. It supports persistent state through mounted directories and allows users to target specific Hermes versions using build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module enables reproducible deployments through declarative configuration of workspace documents and settings. It offers a hybrid management system for skills and integrates with sops-nix for secure secrets handling via systemd.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first control plane designed to orchestrate multiple agent instances with distinct identities and workspaces from a single web application. It manages granular permissions for tools and networks while providing dedicated Telegram and WhatsApp communication channels.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: Targeting headless Ubuntu and Debian environments, this project configures the Hermes Gateway as a reboot-safe systemd service. It is designed for production-ready autonomous execution of recurring AI tasks via cron jobs.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes OTG is a portable distribution that runs from USB drives without requiring host installation or registry modifications. It bundles Python, PortableGit, and rescue tools to support Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes in offline or isolated environments.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a multi-agent LLM framework for financial trading in which specialized agents such as analysts, traders, and risk managers debate to evaluate market conditions. It belongs in this list as an example of role-specialized agents collaborating through debate, and the README notes it is designed for research rather than financial advice.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted orchestration layer for dispatching tasks, running multi-agent workflows, and monitoring spend. It governs task assignment, agent registration, memory browsing, and cost tracking, and exposes these capabilities through a Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API. It can be installed locally via Node.js or deployed with Docker.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Gemini. It keeps persistent agent sessions running in the background via tmux, supports sandboxing with Docker, Podman, and Apple Containers, and offers dashboards with diff review.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: This project is a Control Room-first template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent into specialist teams and automated workflows. It uses a level-based architecture and a task bus pattern for orchestrator-to-specialist delegation and handoffs, and bundles skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: Swarmclaw is a framework for building autonomous AI agent swarms with orchestration, skills, and support for multiple model providers. It supports 23+ LLM providers including OpenAI and Ollama, provides durable agent memory and MCP tool integration, and includes visual org charts for delegating work across agent teams.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a Mission Control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work from a single screen. It presents a Kanban board for tracking task status and review queues, streams agent reasoning and tool execution live, and requires human-in-the-loop verification for every agent-proposed task completion.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized AI agents covering research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. It follows a strict pipeline architecture and includes a Master Orchestrator responsible for routing and coordination, making it a structured pipeline-based entry in this list.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local multi-agent collaboration web system built on Hermes Agent profiles, MCP, ACP, and Hermes Kanban. It orchestrates Leader and Specialist agents for automated task lifecycle management, integrates MCP and ACP for local tool and communication handling, and provides a real-time Web UI for monitoring agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: This meta-harness for Hermes Agent focuses on meta-optimization, automating outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code. It orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 benchmark evaluations and provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking, distinguishing it as an optimization-oriented rather than task-execution framework.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator stages an agent-vs-agent arena in which autonomous AI companies compete for GitHub stars. It orchestrates 9 autonomous agents across two competing companies, using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, and includes a real-time dashboard visualizing agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a fully local multi-model agent framework that runs a Mixture-of-Agents stack on consumer GPUs with Hermes and Ollama and no cloud dependencies. It implements Mixture-of-Agents through parallel model querying and synthesis, uses Hermes for task routing and tool-calling, and is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph provides a local, pre-indexed code knowledge graph that coding agents can query to reduce token usage and tool calls. It connects to agents through an MCP server and automatically syncs the graph when files change. This makes it a fit for Hermes Agent setups where grounding code understanding in a local index matters.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale is a CLI tool for tracking token usage and costs across AI coding agents, including Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, and Gemini. It reads data from each client's local storage paths and offers a submit command for a leaderboard and public profile. It belongs here as a cross-agent accounting utility for developers watching spend.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for inspecting coding-agent API traffic from Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode, among others. It provides a self-contained HTML viewer for exported trace sessions and redacts common authentication headers before recording. This makes it useful for debugging and auditing agent requests without sending traces elsewhere.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor is a real-time widget for token usage, cost, and rate limits that reads Hermes Agent state directly alongside Claude Code, Codex, and other CLIs. It reads local data paths per listed tool and separates token usage, limits, and session details. Multi-device sync and historical usage trends make it a monitoring companion for agent-heavy workflows.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers to help build better UI with AI. It is compatible with any AI provider supporting markdown or general prompting and integrates with Hermes Agent, Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot. It earns a place here as an interface-design aid for agent-assisted development.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. It loads 36 skills and 6 workflows directly into Hermes Agent and coordinates seven specialized agent roles through a CTO loop. It also automates deployment, health checks, and log observation across VPS or local environments.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins offers community CLI skins and themes for the Hermes terminal UI. It customizes banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art banners, with YAML-based configuration for creating themes such as retro DOS and cyberpunk aesthetics. It fits this list as a lightweight personalization layer for Hermes users.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang is a static linter for AI agent configs, tool descriptions, and system prompts that uses HERM v1.1 scoring. It performs scans with no model calls or network access, and its findings name the file and propose a specific fix. It emits JSON, SARIF, and GitLab Code Quality reports, making it useful for CI-friendly validation of agent assets.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments. It belongs here as infrastructure for agent interaction and payments rather than a coding tool.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser built for autonomous agent control via MCP. It has built-in support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other AI providers, plus a supervisor sidebar for managing agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads. It also supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes CCC is a port of the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to the Claude Code Channel. It runs natively in Claude Code without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages organized into two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin auto-captures and auto-recalls context. It fits this list as a memory integration layer for agent workflows.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: A preconfigured Hermes Agent setup that pairs RTK and Caveman templating to cut token usage by 90-99%, aimed at developers who want lower-cost agent runs out of the box. It ships with 40+ pre-configured skills spanning finance, devops, and research, plus automated cross-platform installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: A TAW Agent framework for building scoped Hermes Agents, where each folder carries its own local configuration and skills. It switches between default and scoped agents and supports project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions, making it useful when one workspace needs different agent behavior than another.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: A setup package that gets a hermes-agent stack running in minutes using free models, 29 plugins, and zero cost. It automates installation of hermes-agent alongside 12+ supporting services and offers three scalable deployment tiers, from a minimum viable setup to a production stack, with plugins organized across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: A migration tool for moving from OpenClaw to Hermes Agent, transferring SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives. It maps OpenClaw configs and credentials into Hermes YAML and JSON formats, sets up systemd gateway services, and handles nested auth structures.
entries.observeco/observeco: Self-healing observability for AI agents that discovers, monitors, and auto-recovers multi-agent systems without a cloud dependency. Its native Hermes plugin exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations, and it offers two monitoring modes—zero-token passive analysis and scheduled active probing—while config-aware baselines detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: A voice-enabled personal assistant for Hermes Agent with an open mic and wake word, running fully local with no API keys or accounts. It supports 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro, and adds adaptive turn-taking and barge-in for more natural spoken interaction.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: A deterministic, zero-network local runtime by default, intended to help users make their first genuine dollar online with Hermes Agent. It requires explicit approval for all consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer-previews, and exact-approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: A Hermes memory plugin for MemOS that provides semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It includes tools for searching, adding, and deleting memories, along with a circuit breaker to handle MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: A cross-platform, all-in-one manager for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Gemini CLI, and Hermes Agent. It offers one-click API provider switching and centrally manages MCP, Skills, and Prompts, so users avoid hand-editing JSON, TOML, and YAML configs. It belongs here as the configuration hub that keeps multiple agent CLIs consistent from one place.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: A local open-source cowork app for OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, and other agent CLIs. It supports autonomous multi-step tasks with user approval and file access, includes built-in assistants for generating editable PPT, Word, and Excel files, and enables 24/7 unattended automation via cron and remote access interfaces. Its document-generation and always-on automation make it a distinct productivity workspace rather than just a chat front end.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a browser-based way to use Hermes Agent from the web or a phone. It uses a three-panel layout with a sessions sidebar, chat center, and workspace file browser, and runs the Hermes agent in-process reading HERMES_HOME config. With no build step, framework, or bundler, it stays Python and vanilla JS, making it the minimal, dependency-light web option in this list.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: A desktop companion app for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent. It provides a guided first-run install, connects to a local or remote backend, and offers a streaming chat UI with 22 slash commands. It fits here as the onboarding-focused desktop client for users who want setup handled for them.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: A web dashboard for Hermes Agent covering multi-platform AI chat, session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration for Telegram, Discord, Slack, and WhatsApp. It is a local-first AI workspace for multi-agent chat and workflows, distributed as a desktop app, npm CLI, and Docker, with unified configuration for 10 platform channels. Its analytics and channel-management scope distinguish it from pure chat interfaces.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: A native web workspace combining chat, terminal, memory browser, skills manager, and an inspector panel. It adds Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus an integrated memory browser, skills manager, MCP catalog, and a full workspace file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal. It belongs here as the most operations-oriented workspace for running and inspecting agent activity.
entries.xintaofei/codeg: A collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and others. It ships with fifteen agents built in, lets any ACP agent join, and supports importing, searching, resuming, and handing off session history across desktop, self-hosted, Docker, iOS, and Android. Its cross-agent session aggregation is what sets it apart in this list.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: A native Mac workspace for Hermes built around real SSH, a real terminal, and real session data. It connects directly to local or SSH Hermes hosts and provides native views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs, along with an embedded terminal for shell access and system repair. It stands out as the Mac-native, SSH-first client for managing remote Hermes hosts.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: A Windows-first Chinese desktop app for Hermes Agent built with Tauri, TypeScript, and Rust. It supports Windows and macOS with native window and process management, a built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health check and update capabilities, and UI for chat, memory management, and LaTeX/Markdown rendering. It is the localized, Windows-first option in this collection.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: A Chromium side-panel extension that connects active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime. The side panel supports local, Cloud, or remote Hermes connections and a Bot Mode for agent switching and group chats, while Firefox omits Chromium-only real-tab attach. It earns its place by bringing Hermes into the browser rather than requiring a separate app.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: A native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent from your phone, pairing with a hermes-webui server. It targets iOS 18+, is client-only with the server run by the user, and is free with no analytics or tracking. It is the mobile, privacy-conscious companion for self-hosted Hermes setups.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: A desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. It includes a runtime dashboard for tracking token usage and latency and a live workspace for monitoring code writes and diffs. Its emphasis on model routing and runtime observability distinguishes it from the other desktop clients here.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: A terminal-based consciousness monitor for Hermes, built as an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes. It tracks agent growth, git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, and provides a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: A native macOS session browser and agent cockpit that searches 16 local agent histories in one app. It tracks per-session Codex and Claude quota burn and builds its search index locally with no telemetry.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: A self-hosted web dashboard for the Hermes AI agent stack, offering a browser-based terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and an agent status panel. It includes real-time chat with streaming and tool call visualization, an MCP server control plane for managing server lifecycles, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for tracking agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: A native macOS workspace for Hermes Agent running on Orgo cloud computers and SSH hosts. It provides one-click automated Hermes Agent installation on fresh cloud computers and an integrated WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: A self-hostable mission-control dashboard template that pairs with your own local Hermes agent over a Postgres message bus. It features an approval inbox for requests with side effects and is built with Next.js 16, React 19, Prisma, and Tailwind CSS v4.
entries.liftaris/herm: An alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI. It provides a TUI for chatting and managing Hermes Agent sessions, includes a kanban board for agentic work and task management, and supports managing profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: A React SPA dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0 with a 10-page mobile-first UI that runs locally. It offers terminal chat with streaming responses and file attachment support, dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication for Telegram validation, and background agent spawning with support for five concurrent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: A portable Hermes Agent desktop for Windows 10/11 that requires no install, Docker, or admin rights. It includes 100 tools across 20+ toolsets, and TTS, Music, and ComfyUI extensions auto-install on first use.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: A glassmorphic web interface for Hermes Agent, a self-hosted AI assistant. It combines chat and real-time log streaming with an integrated file browser, task tracking dashboard, and management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: A process monitoring and configuration dashboard for Hermes. It provides a real-time dashboard for session activity and cost tracking, full inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, and read-only monitoring of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: A self-hosted AI workspace with chat, skills, extensions, memory, profiles, and runtime controls. It is chat-first with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards, includes an integrated marketplace for discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, and offers isolated profile management for separate sessions, memory, and API keys.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: A multi-agent Hermes Agent desktop client with specialists, a visual skill store, a PM orchestrator, and streaming chat. It supports orchestrated collaboration between 20 specialized AI agents, a Visual Skill Store with 50+ curated one-click installations, and a native desktop interface with streaming SSE responses and model switching.
